intro: Max pooling discards positions unless the winning locations are saved. Use those switches to place the retained values back into a larger map.
task: Scatter pooled values to distinct flattened output indices and fill all other positions with zero.
requirements: values and switches are matching matrices. output_size is two integer dimensions in 1..64. Each switch is a unique integer index in 0..output_height*output_width-1, using row-major flattening.
Return the output matrix. Reject duplicate switches rather than choosing an overwrite or addition rule. This reconstructs retained maxima only, not the original non-maximum pixels.

Use finite real numeric values of magnitude at most 1e6, excluding boolean inputs. Each array axis has 1..64 entries and at most 65536 elements total unless a stricter bound is stated. Return NumPy arrays for array outputs, preserve caller inputs, and raise ValueError for invalid inputs.

examples.output:

(NumPy arrays shown as lists; rounded to 12 significant digits.)

hints.title: Follow the data
hints.body: Create a zero vector of the total output size, then scatter and reshape.

hints.title: Check the boundary
hints.body: Checking uniqueness makes the result independent of traversal order.

explanation: Saved pooling switches preserve where the selected maxima came from. Unpooling can therefore produce a sparse spatial representation aligned with the earlier feature map.
Most source values were discarded during pooling and cannot be recovered. Zero-filled positions explicitly represent that missing information rather than an inverse of the entire pooling operation.
